headline: Public hearing on Elite Indoor Gun Range license renewal at 371 Rose Hill Road, and $1,892,556.56 in new high school technology contracts.
summary: Many routine license renewals and contracts are on the consent agenda. Other business includes a snow shoveling rule change, a Revolutionary War memorial, and a Saugatucket Road culvert contract.
items: Closed executive session on acquiring, leasing, or disposing of public property
Swearing-in of Alfred E. Bucco as police chief
Interviews for six board and commission applicants
Consent agenda: 14 routine items, including two contracts, a $2,687.00 tax abatement, and license renewals
Road race license for the Mews Tavern Gear N' Beer 5K on November 22, 2026
Class F 19-hour beverage license for the same race, for South County Health
Temporary mass gathering permit for Whiskey Wonderland at 1425 Kingstown Road, December 11 and 12, 2026
Public hearing on renewal of Elite Indoor Gun Range license at 371 Rose Hill Road
Affirm police chief appointment of Alfred E. Bucco, effective November 9, 2026
Approve final roster and inscription for the Brave Men as Ever Fought companion memorial
Order of notice for public hearing on snow shoveling exemption changes to Chapter 16
Amend GZA Environmental culvert engineering contract to $132,289
Library security camera contract with K&M Communications, $44,086.85
High school technology contracts, $1,892,556.56 total, funded by bond referendum
Town Manager report on high school construction, first-quarter general fund results, and November 3 election
Resignation of Terrence Simpson as registered agent for South Kingstown school funds trustees, effective December 31, 2026
Pond Street residents' request for a three-way stop sign and speed limit signs

10. Public Comment - 30 Minutes 
Rule 10A. for the conduct of the meetings of the South Kingstown Town Council: Members 
of the public shall be entitled to speak at regular meetings during any period designated on 
the agenda for public comment, once, for a period of five minutes, or longer at the 
discretion of the President, and at other times when invited to do so by the President. The 
public shall address their comments to the question under debate as indicated on the 
agenda. Pursuant to RI General Laws §42-46-6(b), public comment regarding subject 
matter not on the agenda but received during the public participation portion of a meeting 
shall be for information purposes only and may not be voted on except where necessary to 
address an unexpected occurrence that requires immediate action to protect the public or 
to refer the matter to an appropriate committee or to another body or official.

South Kingstown Chief of Police, effective November 9, 2026.
Posted on 11/5/2026 
 B. A resolution approving the final roster of sixty (60) Revolutionary War era patriots 
of African, Indigenous, and multiracial heritage and the precise inscription

the 1932 Flagstaff War Memorial at the Historic Hazard School site, as set forth 
in the accompanying documentation dated October 20 and October 21, 2026, 
and authorizing the project sponsors to proceed with preparation of the final 
monument engraving layout and proof, subject to final verification of consistency

Services to the Town Manager dated November 4, 2026, entitled “Brave Men as 
Ever Fought Companion Memorial – Approval of Final Roster of Names and 
Monument Inscription.” 
 C. A resolution authorizing the Town Clerk to advertise for Order of Notice a Public

Chapter 16 - Streets and Sidewalks, Section 16-1 - Definitions, to refine the 
eligibility criteria for a snow shoveling exemption, as attached.

Environmental, Inc., 188 Valley Street, Suite 300, Providence, RI 02909 for 
consulting engineering and design services in an amount from $107,789.00 to 
$132,289 which includes an additional $5,000 contingency, and as further 
described in a memorandum from the Public Services Director to the Town 
Manager, dated November 2, 2026, entitled "Contract Amendment – 
Saugatucket Road Culvert Engineering Services."  Funding for the Town's 
additional required matching funds would come from the Town's Grant Matching 
Fund (fund-403). 
 E. 
A resolution authorizing a contract award to K&M Communications Corporation, 
doing business as The Navicon Group, located at 750 Washington St, South 
Easton, MA, 02375, for the provision, installation, and licensing of cameras at 
Peace Dale and Kingston Libraries in the amount of $44,086.85, with a 
contingency of $5,000. Included in the price is the annual license cost of 
$4,295.25; which the Town would like to extend a three-year renewal cost, not to 
exceed a ten percent (10%) increase over the previous year, as detailed in a 
memorandum from the Director of Technology to the Town Manager dated 
October 29, 2026, titled "Contract Award for Security Cameras at Public Library 
Locations."  Funding is available in existing capital reserves of the town, a 
combination of funding from the library ($29,086.85) and Information Technology 
($20,000). 
 
 F. A resolution authorizing the Town Manager to award contracts to multiple 
vendors for the purchase, installation, configuration, and integration of technology 
equipment and infrastructure associated with the construction of the new South 
Kingstown High School, in a base amount of $1,720,505.96, together with a 10% 
project contingency of $172,050.60, for a total amount not to exceed 
$1,892,556.56, utilizing applicable Rhode Island Master Price Agreements, 
cooperative purchasing contracts, and sole-source procurement procedures, as
Posted on 11/5/2026 
further described in a memorandum from the Deputy Town Manager/Director of 
Administrative Services to the Town Manager dated November 2, 2026, entitled 
“Authorization to Award Multiple Contracts for Technology Equipment and 
Infrastructure – New South Kingstown High School.”  Funding is available via 
fund-435 (New High School Project) and backed by the voter approved bond 
referendum.
